findings.title: Many render-blocking resources in <head>
findings.description: 29 synchronous scripts/stylesheets (0 script(s), 29 stylesheet(s)) load in <head> before the browser can start painting the page.
findings.recommendation: Add async/defer to non-critical scripts, inline small critical CSS, and load the rest of the stylesheet asynchronously.

findings.title: Large HTML document
findings.description: The initial HTML document is 563KB. This is the document alone, before any linked CSS/JS/images even start downloading.
findings.recommendation: Reduce inline scripts/styles and repeated markup; consider server-side pagination for very long pages.

findings.title: Images missing explicit dimensions
findings.description: 24 of 24 images have no width/height attributes, so the browser can't reserve space for them before they load — a common cause of layout shift.
findings.recommendation: Add width and height attributes (or aspect-ratio in CSS) to every so the browser reserves the right amount of space.

findings.title: Redundant ARIA role
findings.description: https://github.com has 2 element(s) with a role attribute that just restates the element's own native role (e.g. role="button" on a <button>), which adds nothing and is one more place for markup to drift out of sync.
findings.recommendation: Remove the redundant role attribute and rely on the element's native semantics.

findings.title: TLS certificate expiring soon
findings.description: The certificate for github.com expires in 23 day(s) (not_after: Oct  2 20:44:39 2026 GMT).
findings.recommendation: Schedule renewal now, ideally via an automated process, so expiry never becomes an incident.

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy header
findings.description: https://github.com does not send a `Permissions-Policy` header, so every powerful browser API (camera, microphone, geolocation, USB, etc.) stays available to any script running on the page — including third-party scripts — with no opt-out declared.
findings.recommendation: Add a `Permissions-Policy` header that explicitly disables APIs the site doesn't use, e.g. `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`.

findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header
findings.description: https://github.com does not send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`, leaving the page's window reachable from cross-origin popups it opens (or that open it), which can enable cross-window attacks like tabnabbing-style reference leaks.
findings.recommendation: Add `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` unless the site specifically relies on cross-origin window references.

findings.title: Server software/version disclosed in response headers
findings.description: https://github.com exposes implementation details via response headers (server: github.com). This makes it easier for an attacker to look up known vulnerabilities for the exact software version in use.
findings.recommendation: Suppress or generalize these headers at the server/proxy level (e.g. `server_tokens off;` in nginx, removing X-Powered-By in most frameworks).

findings.title: Primary navigation has a large number of links
findings.description: https://github.com's main navigation contains 61 links (more than 10). A long flat list of top-level choices makes it harder for visitors to scan and pick the right one, and is a common sign navigation would benefit from grouping into a dropdown/mega-menu structure.
findings.recommendation: Group related links under a smaller number of top-level categories, using dropdowns/submenus for the rest.

findings.title: Button(s) with no visible or accessible label
findings.description: https://github.com has 1 button-like element(s) with no text content, value, or aria-label. Visitors — and especially screen reader users, who hear nothing at all announced — have no way to know what the control does.
findings.recommendation: Give every button real visible text describing its action, or an aria-label if it's icon-only.

findings.title: Interactive elements packed together with no spacing markup
findings.description: https://github.com has a run of 5 links/buttons in a row (e.g. Code, Plan, Collaborate, ...) with no whitespace or separating element between them in the markup. Without CSS spacing explicitly compensating, tightly packed tap targets are a common source of accidental mis-taps, especially on touch devices.
findings.recommendation: Add visible spacing (margin/gap) between adjacent interactive elements — a `gap` on a flex/grid container is the simplest fix — and confirm on an actual mobile viewport that targets don't touch.

findings.title: Body copy scores as hard to read
findings.description: https://github.com's visible text scores 29/100 on the Flesch Reading Ease scale (very difficult to read) — driven by long sentences and/or long, multi-syllable words. General audiences typically read most comfortably in the 60-70 range (roughly an 8th-grade reading level).
findings.recommendation: Shorten sentences, prefer plain words over jargon where the audience doesn't require it, and break up dense paragraphs — aim for a Flesch score in the 60s for general-audience content.

findings.title: Images missing width/height attributes
findings.description: 24 of 24 image(s) on https://github.com have no width/height attributes (or aspect-ratio style): https://github.githubassets.com/assets/particles-170bd1fd231f4669.png, //images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/g1XhuDG7foMyNWIEIpGJj/b40a790b854d0803704deb7905b1bd82/logo-duolingo-14477f9e54a6.svg, //images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/6Qr8Snm4JceoMFRJhapgFa/802ded1d2c486a9d0a4c073d9f8f38f4/logo-gartner-aa8c2e452b64.svg, //images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/1Dt1ncaR6ZM4dQvknFzfBI/e5c2092be5bd53881622eced4fd37564/accordion-1-ce487d44c0bf.webp, //images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/1uXZYDy7dMcH9QwxuAU06F/1cb167cc60d725b8cf7089faf9a4ed06/accordion-2-730955545f07.webp. Without a reserved size, the browser doesn't know how much space to leave for the image before it loads, so surrounding content jumps once it arrives — a direct Cumulative Layout Shift contributor.
findings.recommendation: Add width and height attributes (or a CSS aspect-ratio) matching the image's intrinsic size so the browser can reserve layout space up front.

findings.title: First image on the page is lazy-loaded
findings.description: https://github.com's first in document order has loading="lazy". This image is the one most likely to be above the fold and the Largest Contentful Paint element — lazy-loading it defers its fetch instead of prioritizing it, which typically hurts LCP rather than page performance overall.
findings.recommendation: Remove loading="lazy" from the first/hero image (and consider fetchpriority="high" on it instead); reserve lazy loading for images further down the page.

findings.title: Broken image sources found
findings.description: 22 image(s) on https://github.com returned an error status: https://github.githubassets.com/assets/particles-170bd1fd231f4669.png (403), https://images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/g1XhuDG7foMyNWIEIpGJj/b40a790b854d0803704deb7905b1bd82/logo-duolingo-14477f9e54a6.svg (403), https://images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/6Qr8Snm4JceoMFRJhapgFa/802ded1d2c486a9d0a4c073d9f8f38f4/logo-gartner-aa8c2e452b64.svg (403), https://images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/1Dt1ncaR6ZM4dQvknFzfBI/e5c2092be5bd53881622eced4fd37564/accordion-1-ce487d44c0bf.webp (403), https://images.ctfassets.net/8aevphvgewt8/1uXZYDy7dMcH9QwxuAU06F/1cb167cc60d725b8cf7089faf9a4ed06/accordion-2-730955545f07.webp (403) and 17 more.
findings.recommendation: Fix the src URL or replace/remove the image so visitors don't see a broken-image icon.

findings.title: No responsive breakpoints found in inline CSS
findings.description: https://github.com has <style> block CSS but no @media query anywhere in it, suggesting the visible styling doesn't change across screen sizes. (An external stylesheet could still carry breakpoints — this only inspects inline and <style>-block CSS.)
findings.recommendation: Add @media breakpoints (or confirm they exist in an external stylesheet) so layout, font sizes, and spacing adapt for narrow screens.

findings.title: Many render-blocking resources for a mobile connection
findings.description: The page references 48 script/stylesheet tags that can block first render. On a fast desktop connection this is often invisible; on a throttled mobile connection each blocking request adds a full round-trip before the page can paint.
findings.recommendation: Defer or async non-critical scripts, inline small critical CSS, and combine or lazy-load the rest so the mobile round-trip cost is paid by fewer requests.

findings.title: High image count on a single page
findings.description: The page loads 24 tags. On mobile, each additional image competes for limited bandwidth on a connection that's often both slower and metered compared to desktop broadband.
findings.recommendation: Lazy-load below-the-fold images (see images/lazyload.py) and consider pagination or a "load more" pattern for long image-heavy pages.

findings.title: No CAPTCHA or bot-mitigation widget detected on a sensitive form
findings.description: https://github.com has 2 form(s) that look like login, signup, contact, or similar (by field type or form identity), but no recognizable CAPTCHA/bot-mitigation script (reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Turnstile, FunCaptcha) was found on the page. Forms like these are common targets for automated spam and credential-stuffing traffic.
findings.recommendation: Add a CAPTCHA or equivalent bot-mitigation step to forms that collect credentials or contact info, or confirm equivalent protection is applied at the server/WAF level instead.

findings.title: No cookie-consent banner detected
findings.description: https://github.com shows no recognizable consent banner or CMP markup. If this page sets non-essential cookies, this is likely a GDPR/ePrivacy compliance gap.
findings.recommendation: Add a consent banner (a CMP like OneTrust/Cookiebot, or a compliant custom implementation) before any non-essential cookies are set.

findings.title: Scripts are not held back until consent is given
findings.description: https://github.com does not appear to block non-essential scripts before consent (based on the page's own declared Consent Mode default only — not independently verified).
findings.recommendation: Gate non-essential scripts (analytics, ads, embeds) behind an explicit consent check rather than loading them unconditionally.

findings.title: Reject button could not be located to test
findings.description: https://github.com: no clickable Reject/Decline control was found in the rendered page, so this behaviour could not be runtime-verified.
findings.recommendation: Confirm a reject control is rendered and reachable without JavaScript errors.

findings.title: Accept button could not be located to test
findings.description: https://github.com: no clickable Accept/Allow control was found in the rendered page, so this behaviour could not be runtime-verified.
findings.recommendation: Confirm an accept control is rendered and reachable without JavaScript errors.

findings.title: AI review: Consent is the biggest opportunity
findings.description: Based on the other module scores, consent (89/100) is where https://github.com would benefit most from attention first.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize the consent findings from this audit before the next run.
